connections.description: Both papers address the fundamental challenge of adapting large language models for low-resource languages through supervised fine-tuning (SFT), using distinct language families (Azerbaijani and African languages) as case studies. The Azerbaijani study reviews SFT challenges including data scarcity and tokenization problems, while the African languages thesis establishes INJONGO benchmark and demonstrates SFT effectively adapts decoder-only LLMs to downstream tasks.

evidence.quote: Large Language Models have shown capabilities in natural language processing tasks. Their performance drops drastically on low-resource languages that lack large annotated corpora. We look at the challenges of fine-tuning Large Language Models for low-resource languages with Azerbaijani as a case study.

We examine data scarcity, morphological complexity, tokenization problems and domain gaps that make model adaptation harder. We also review methods like data augmentation, cross-lingual pre-training and transfer learning and assess how well they work for Azerbaijani.

Despite remarkable advances in Large Language Models (LLMs), African languagesremain critically underserved by the current training and adaptation pipeline. This thesisaddresses the fundamental bottlenecks in adapting LLMs for low-resource languagesthrough a unified two-stage investigation: benchmarking via Supervised Fine-Tuning(SFT) and foundational adaptation via Continued Pre-Training (CPT).

Our experiments yield two key findings: (1) SFT effectively adaptsdecoder-only LLMs to downstream tasks, demonstrating the viability of task-specificalignment; and (2) encoder models pre-trained on African languages (e.g., AfroXLMR-76L)with SFT dramatically outperform those without such exposure.
